newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran arrests protesters at Tehran German mission.
newsitem.headline: Iran arrests protesters at Tehran German mission.

text.p: Iranian riot police on Monday arrested students protesting at the German embassy in Iran who said they would seize the mission unless Bonn apologised for a court verdict accusing Iran's leadership of ordering political killings, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.

"The special guards protecting the German embassy in Tehran arrested some of the university students who attempted to break into the security line of the embassy," IRNA said. Police have surrounded the diplomatic mission and erected barriers to prevent demonstrators from reaching the building.

The agency said: "A spokesman of the students warned the embassy officials that they would seize the embassy unless the German government make a formal apology to the Iranian nation and retreat from hostility against Iran."
IRNA said the demonstration caused a traffic jam in the streets near the embassy as police tried to prevent protesters from reaching the compound.

It was the third demonstration held at the German embassy in central Tehran since Friday, a day after a Berlin court sentenced to jail three Lebanese and an Iranian for the 1992 killing of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin. The court said senior Iranian leaders had ordered the killing.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the killings which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani has condemned the verdict as provoked by Israel and the United States, but added that a diplomatic row over the ruling was a "passing storm".
